hook: This rocket engine fired for 630 seconds straight.
narration: This rocket engine fired for more than ten minutes straight.
It's an RS-25, the kind that helps launch NASA's Moon rocket, on a test stand in Mississippi.
Operators ran it for six hundred thirty seconds, longer than the five hundred it must fire at launch.
[short pause] They also pushed it to one hundred thirteen percent power.
Four of these fire together at launch, making up to two million pounds of thrust.
The extra time and power give the engines a margin of safety.
outcome: The engine fired for the full six hundred thirty seconds.
title: Rocket engine fired for 10 minutes straight
description:
On May 10, 2023, NASA fired an RS-25 certification engine for 630 seconds on the Fred Haise Test Stand at Stennis Space Center in Mississippi, longer than the 500 seconds the engines must fire to help launch the Space Launch System rocket.
